atoms.a: What are the body parts that carry blood around the body called?

feedback.finish: Blood vessels act like a system of pipes, carrying blood around the body. There are three different types: arteries, veins and capillaries.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

hint.text:
A useful way to remember the direction of blood flow is with alliteration!
Arteries = Away from the heart.
hint.sound: A useful way to remember the direction of blood flow is with alliteration! Arteries, Away from the heart.

atoms.text: The role of the arteries is to carry blood away from the heart. The arteries take oxygen-poor blood to the lungs and transport oxygen-rich blood around the body.

atoms.a: In which direction do the arteries carry blood?
Where do the arteries transport oxygen-poor blood to?

atoms.text: The veins return blood to the heart. They carry oxygen-rich blood to the heart from the lungs and oxygen-poor blood to the heart from the body .

atoms.a: In which direction do the veins carry blood?
Where do the veins transport oxygen-rich blood?

instruction.text: Label the arteries and veins on the diagram.

hint.text: Remember that arteries carry blood away from the heart, and veins carry blood towards it!

atoms.a: What are the smallest blood vessels in the body called?

feedback.finish: Capillaries are a network of tiny blood vessels that connect the smallest branches of the arteries and veins.

atoms.b: The walls of the ((++capillaries intestines)) are one cell thick. This means that substances can easily pass between the blood and the body’s ((++cells bacteria)).
Oxygen passes from the bloodstream into the body’s cells through the capillaries’ ((++thin thick)) walls.
Carbon dioxide passes from the body’s cells into the bloodstream so that it can be transported to the ((++lungs eyes)) and breathed out.
